title: Measuring What Matters: Connecting AI Ethics Evaluations to System Attributes, Hazards, and Harms

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing and categorizing mathematical and statistical measures (e.g., word embedding association tests, cosine similarity, diversity scores, person prominence) that quantify stereotype reinforcement, imbalanced group representation, and underrepresentation of identity groups in AI systems.

Reviewing measures (e.g., disparate impact, demographic parity, treatment equality) that quantify the unequal distribution of beneficial or erroneous system outputs, resources, or opportunities across different social and demographic groups.

Reviewing measures (e.g., group-level differences in precision, F1-score, exposure) that capture disparities in model performance and user experience quality across different demographic and identity groups.
Reviewing measures capturing upstream design choices that lead to outcome disparities, such as class imbalance and conditional disparity in dataset labels across protected groups.
